/-!
# Erdős Problem 234

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/234](https://www.erdosproblems.com/234)
-/

open Real Set
open scoped NNReal

namespace Erdos234

/--
Is it true that for all `c ≥ 0`, the density `f c` of integers for which
`(p (n + 1) - p n) / log n < c` exists and is a continuous function of `c`?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_234 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ f : ℝ≥0 → ℝ, Continuous f ∧
    ∀ c : ℝ≥0, HasDensity {n : ℕ | primeGap n / log n < c} (f c) := by
  sorry

end Erdos234

reformulations.difference: Nat.nth indexes primes from zero, whereas the customary source notation indexes them from one. Lean also includes n = 0 and n = 1, where its logarithm/division conventions make the quotient zero.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Write b_n = (p_{n+1} - p_n)/log n using one-based primes, and let a_n be Lean's quotient. For n ≥ 2, a_n = b_{n+1}·log(n+1)/log n. Shifting a sequence by one preserves the densities of its sublevel sets, and the positive factor log(n+1)/log n tends to 1. For c > 0 and 0 < ε < 1, eventually the sublevel set of a_n at c lies between those of b_{n+1} at c/(1+ε) and c/(1−ε). Continuity of the proposed density function squeezes the limiting density to f(c). Applying the same argument to the reciprocal factor proves the converse. At c = 0 the sublevel sets are empty, and the finitely many exceptional initial indices do not affect density. Thus the full continuous-density assertion is equivalent. The finite-prefix equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/finite_prefix.lean; the full rescaling equivalence was checked mathematically, not formalized.
